dedupe_keys.name: urban nature atlas database of nature based solutions in cities

description: The Urban Nature Atlas is a database of nature-based solution interventions in cities, built to analyse socio-economic and innovation patterns of urban nature-based solutions and to share examples between cities. It covers more than 1,000 examples, starting from a systematic survey of interventions in 100 European cities and later extended to cases outside Europe, with entries describing goals and impact profiles. It was developed by the NATURVATION project, funded by the European Union's Horizon 2020 programme under grant agreement 730243, and moved after the project to a permanent home at una.city, where all entries were reviewed and updated between July and November 2020 and a new search engine and case submission were added. The database is available free online through the atlas search interface; no licence or bulk download was seen, and the una.city site refused automated requests when read today, so current size and terms were not checked there. Caveats: entries are compiled case descriptions of varying depth, not measured performance data. It supports benchmarking and siting of urban green-blue infrastructure and evidence gathering for climate adaptation planning; a related record is the Oppla nature-based solutions repository.
